_doc: DESIGN-THEME-UNIVERSAL-COVERAGE-W1 R1 — the declared exemption set for the theme-region
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. DESIGN-SURFACE-TOKENS-W1 made every EXISTING page take its colours
from the generated THEME region, and gated the nine retired navy literals. But its --check
only ever flagged a page that carried a Tailwind signature OUTSIDE the markers, or that was
marked and had dropped the design stylesheet. Measured at 75ba70a: a page with NO Tailwind
and NO markers was skipped by the loop entirely (build_theme.mjs `if (!outside) continue`),
so an author could ship a plain <style>-only page in any colour and every gate stayed green.
That is the same hole the footer injector had twice — a page silently outside the target set
— and it is closed the same proven way: targets are DERIVED, and the only thing a human
maintains is the far smaller set of pages that must NOT carry the region, each with its
reason in DATA. An exemption that lives only in a code comment gets 'fixed' by a future wave
enforcing the contract; one that lives here has to be argued with.
THE TARGET SET IS THE INJECTOR'S OWN ANSWER. `glob` below declares the landing half and is
ASSERTED against targets() rather than re-derived from — a second derivation of 'what is a
page' is a second thing that can drift, and the gate would then disagree with the writer
about exactly the files nobody is looking at. docs-src/template.html joins it from targets()
itself. A stale exemption — one naming a file that no longer exists, or one that DOES carry
both markers and the loader — is itself a FAIL: it silently shrinks coverage.

exempt.reason: HTML FRAGMENT — it is the canonical design loader itself, injected INTO the <head> of other pages. It carries no <html>, no <head> and no <body>, so a THEME region here would be pasted a second time into every host page that already has one. Same file, same reason, as the one row in ops/footer-coverage-config.json.
